question.worked_solution:
Let us consider the *squared* distance $S$ between $(2,1)$ and a general point $P(x,y)$:

$$
S=(x-2)^{2}+(y-1)^{2}
$$

We require that the point $P$ lies on the curve $y=\sqrt{6x+7}+1.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}S(x) & =(x-2)^{2}+(y-1)^{2} \\  & =(x-2)^{2}+(\sqrt{6x+7}+1-1)^{2} \\  & =(x-2)^{2}+6x+7 \\  & ={x}^{2}-4x+4+6x+7 \\  & ={x}^{2}+2x+11.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the minimum distance, we take the first derivative of $S(x)$ and equate it to zero. This gives the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}^{′}(x)=2x+2 & =0 \\ 2x & =-2 \\ x & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

We can see that ${S}^{″}(x)=2>0.$ Therefore, $x=-1$ is a minimum of $S.$

So, the squared distance (and therefore the actual distance) is minimized when $x=-1.$
